newsitem.title: POLAND: Polish zloty slips vs basket, seen rebounding.
newsitem.headline: Polish zloty slips vs basket, seen rebounding.

text.p: The Polish zloty dipped against the currency basket in early Thursday trade as banks lenghtned positions cut yesterday, but dealers said the local unit was bound to return to resistance levels later today.
"Banks closed short positions by taking dollars from the market...but the zloty should return to 2.5 percent from parity later today," said Karol Zaluski, dealer at ING Bank in Warsaw.
At 0830 GMT the zloty was at 2.44/2.41 percent from parity, down from 2.52/2.48 percent at 0705.
It was at 3.1448/48 to the dollar, down from 3.1435/45 at opening and at 1.8575/82 to the mark, down from 1.8550/65.

Polish banks cut currency positions on Wednesday in order to place more cash on higher yielding zloty deposits over the week-end. The value date for Thursday's spot transactions is May 20, because of a German national holiday on Monday.
On the money market one-day rates fell further as banks wanted to place surplus cash on the market after building up average reserve positions in the early stages of the month.
Overnight and tomorrow/next offers slipped to 21.85/21.95 percent from opening's 21.70/22.20 and 21.80/22.25 despite the central bank's 300 million zloty reverse repo offer.
